categories.name: Static Clicking
categories.description: Your score is how little time passes between kills, so flick straight at each target, fix it with one small correction if you need to, and be looking at the next target before you click.

categories.name: Dynamic Clicking
categories.description: The targets are moving, so stay on each one for a split second until you're sure you're on it before you click, and don't let a sudden change of direction drag your crosshair with it. On targets that take several hits, move with them until the last click.

categories.name: Precise Tracking
categories.description: Stay smooth and keep your crosshair in the middle of the target the whole time, moving with it in one steady motion and using your arm on long strafes. If your aim gets shaky or you keep losing the target, drop to an easier version.

categories.name: Reactive Tracking
categories.description: React to where the target goes instead of guessing, and sit slightly on the side it's moving away from so you have room when it turns. Stay relaxed, because jittery aim usually means you're tensing up, and if you catch yourself predicting, play an easier version for a while.

categories.name: Speed Switching
categories.description: Hold fire and get to the next target as fast as you can in a straight line, without flicking past it. Kill each target fully before you move, and start finding the next one while you finish the current one.

categories.name: Evasive Switching
categories.description: Focus on movement reading, sustained contact and clean transfers. Start with larger and slower targets, then add tighter movement, more distance and regeneration.

thresholds.note: Every threshold in this season is predicted, not sampled: no scenario in it has a KovaaK's board yet. Each was read off the board the difficulty model predicts from the scenario file, at the same ladder percentiles season 1 cuts from real boards. They are seeds to be recut from Apogee's own runs, and every one says so in its source.
